links.outcome: Detection of hallucinated LLM outputs by an automated classifier layer across medical tasks and models
links.effect: CHECK reduced Llama-3-70B hallucinations from 31% to 0.3% in oncology trial QA; detection AUCs 0.95–0.98 across tasks and models.
links.quote: This capability to discern hallucination generalized across diverse medical tasks (reasoning and education, patient and physician dialogue, radiology report summarization) and a suite of leading open-weight and commercial models (e.g., GPT-4o, DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Llama-70B, GPT-o3, GPT-5), achieving detection AUCs of 0.95–0.98.

links.outcome: Hallucination rate when outputs are integrated with structured open clinical knowledge plus a classifier
links.effect: Hallucinations fell from 31% to 0.3% in Llama-3-70B on oncology trial physician QA; risk driven below accepted clinical error thresholds.
links.quote: By systematically driving hallucination risk below accepted clinical error thresholds, CHECK provides a scalable and plug-and-play solution to enable the reliable deployment of LLMs in medicine and other mission-critical domains.

unlisted_practices: Using hallucination probability from token entropy and ensemble KL divergence to guide iterative refinement of LLM answers

screen.practice: model-agnostic hallucination detection safety layer suppressing unsafe outputs
screen.reason: The paper develops and evaluates CHECK, a model-agnostic post-hoc safety guardrail / output filter layered onto existing LLMs to detect and suppress clinical hallucinations across medical tasks.

primary.practice: plug-and-play safety layer / output filter for hallucination detection
